title: IR0 through time
subtitle: Milestones on the path to a usable Unix-like system — not a release changelog.

milestones.label: First boot
milestones.summary: Kernel reaches userspace init. No shell yet — proof the boot chain and syscall surface are alive.

milestones.label: First ring 3 process
milestones.summary: User mode entry with a real CR3 and iretq. Everything after this is “a program on IR0”, not kernel self-test.

milestones.label: fork / exec
milestones.summary: Processes become composable: shell can spawn children and replace their image.

milestones.label: musl libc
milestones.summary: Real POSIX userspace — printf, malloc, pthread path — without rewriting every program for IR0.

milestones.label: BusyBox
milestones.summary: ash, ls, cat on a MINIX rootfs. The machine becomes operable from a prompt.

milestones.label: runit PID 1
milestones.summary: Service supervision replaces one-shot init harnesses. Persistent product shape.

milestones.label: Persistent installation
milestones.summary: disk.img survives reboot; first-boot account creation on real rootfs.

milestones.label: Doom
milestones.summary: Fullscreen client on /dev/fb0 + input — graphics tier proof, not a toy blit.

milestones.label: ARM64 userspace
milestones.summary: Same ABI story on a second architecture — not a second kernel rewrite for every feature.

milestones.label: TinyX root window
milestones.image_note: Historic gray root-window capture reserved for this milestone — pedagogically more honest than a polished desktop mock.
milestones.summary: Unmodified TinyX/KDrive on IR0 Linux UAPI. Third-party software exposed a read(2) contract bug — fixed in the kernel, not in X.
What comes next is whatever the next smoke turns green.
